implementation: CoverGeometryManager now returns its damage factor along with scaled damage. MissileManager stores the factor in HitData for direct ranged WeaponAttack hits against players and creatures. DamageInfoData and legacy PerformRecoveryPacket emit nonzero factors as Python float, retaining integer zero for hits with no cover calculation.
verification: Focused .NET 5 tests passed 16/16: BootcampCoverGeometryTests checks full/partial/clear factors from original sandbag meshes; CombatDamageTests checks a 0.5 factor in weapon recovery; LightningEffectTests checks nonzero float factors and original zero shape in twelve-field DamageInfo. The first no-Warrior replay was invalid: RequestSwitchToCharacterInSlot arrived at 18:54:14.818 before content rules finished loading at 18:54:17.561; no private instance was created, so there were no placed Thrax. In the corrected copied-client replay, content rules loaded at 19:03:39.129 before the client started and private instance 2 of context 1985 was created for character 1 at 19:04:11.959. With only staged Warrior 198691 omitted, six Thrax placements fired at Alden behind the sandbags. The server logged 192 Cover trace events, all blocked 9/9, using the inferred 0.25 factor. Original-client screenshot covered-hit-1.png shows red -3/-4 damage numbers and a yellow directional arc; the recovered directionalhitwindow.pyo selects DirectionalHitIndicator_Low for a factor from 0.2 through below 0.6. This verifies that the client accepts and displays the copied-server low-cover feedback. It does not establish the final-live server multiplier, exact geometry algorithm or encounter pacing. Recovered client player message 1171 explicitly describes orange/yellow damage indicators near the targeting reticule when incoming damage is reduced by cover; greeting 574 names walls and sandbags. This supports identifying the screenshot yellow arc as cover feedback rather than an unrelated hit effect.
unverified: Final-live server sample locations, damage/cover factor and rounding; cover feedback on abilities and melee; sustained UI behavior outside the staged sandbag diagnostic. The copied-world diagnostic omits the staged Warrior only to expose incoming player hits and is not a reconstruction of the retail encounter.
